title: Narrow ResourceSearch requests to Fields + FIELD_VALUES for tree-only queries
answers: How to make a folder/resource search request fetch only the fields it needs
How to reduce payload size when searching unified storage for parent-folder info
body:
Symptom: folder-tree build-out from unified storage pulls full resource rows when only the parent-folder relationship is needed.
Fix pattern: set ResourceSearchRequest.Fields to the minimal field list (e.g. []string{resource.SEARCH_FIELD_FOLDER}) and ResultFormat to resourcepb.ResourceSearchRequest_FIELD_VALUES so the server returns only those field values instead of full RESOURCE_TABLE rows.
Constraints: the decoding side must still handle RESOURCE_TABLE as a fallback (see sibling note on decode branching); this pattern is for read paths that only need specific indexed field values, not for full-resource retrieval.
applies: callers of resourcepb.ResourceSearchRequest in pkg/services/authz/rbac/store/folder_store.go and similar unified-storage search integrations
says: Folder tree loading fetches too much resource data
How to reduce data payload when searching folder structure
Resource search pulls full data when only paths needed
Storage folder tree building downloads unnecessary resource information
Minimize bandwidth for parent folder relationship queries in storage
search: ResourceSearch requests for tree-only queries must narrow Fields and set ResultFormat to FIELD_VALUES to avoid pulling full resource rows. In pkg/services/authz/rbac/store/folder_store.go:listFoldersViaSearch, set ResourceSearchRequest.Fields to the minimal field list (e.g. []string{resource.SEARCH_FIELD_FOLDER}) and ResultFormat to resourcepb.ResourceSearchRequest_FIELD_VALUES so the server returns only indexed field values instead of full RESOURCE_TABLE rows. The decoding side must still handle RESOURCE_TABLE as a fallback for compatibility. Applies to callers of resourcepb.ResourceSearchRequest in pkg/services/authz/rbac/store/folder_store.go and similar unified-storage search integrations that only need specific indexed fields, not full-resource retrieval.
